svg.title: Erebus architecture: Protocol 5 and wire v3
svg.desc: Agent requests pass through Python to the Rust CLI and STRK20 pool. Encrypted messages use five zero-amount notes. Settlement applies acceptance and payment together. The pool key is visible to the prover, preflight RPC, and pool auditor.
svg.text: EREBUS
Private settlement and negotiation infrastructure for AI agents.
Protocol 5 · wire v3 · Starknet / STRK20
1. Request path
Agent
Chooses terms
MCP server
13 tools · Python
Python SDK
Passes key paths
Rust CLI
Reads keys, signs
STRK20 pool
Verifies proof
2. Encrypted messages in public note salts
Each offer, counteroffer, or acceptance uses five zero-amount notes.
Message fields: type 8b · replyTo 32b · createdAt 40b · amount 128b · deadline 64b · memoHash 128b.
Wire v3 adds a 64-bit deal ID. AES-256-GCM-SIV protects the message contents.
The frame and tag use 592 of 595 payload bits. A derived keystream masks the three spare bits.
Value notes use random salts. Structured salts are used only on zero-amount notes.
3. One deal
Both identities register and fund public fees. The payer also needs shielded payment notes.
Each side opens its channel direction. They exchange offers and counteroffers through the pair.
Only the payer accepts and settles: the call spends the caller’s notes.
Settlement writes five acceptance notes, one payment note, and a change note when needed.
The pool applies the acceptance and payment together. The channel pair remains open for more deals.
4. What the proof checks
The pool checks spending authority, value conservation, and that input notes are not spent twice.
The Rust client checks that the payment amount matches the accepted offer.
The pool circuit does not understand offer terms and does not prove that equality.
Settlement does not verify delivery or hold funds in escrow.
5. Disclosure and observers
A wire-v3 grant lets one registered recipient read one deal until expiry. It gives no spending authority.
MCP writes the grant to a file. Creating or opening it submits no transaction.
Expiry cannot erase data already read. Historical wire-v1/v2 grants have broader bearer access.
Public observers see counterparty addresses, submitting accounts, transaction timing, and note counts.
6. Key exposure
Python passes file paths. Rust reads the account signing key and the pool private key.
The prover and preflight RPC receive the pool key. The submitted transaction does not include it.
Registration encrypts the pool key to the pool auditor, which can read the identity’s pool history.
This software is experimental and has no independent security review.
Sources: main Erebus repository · wire.rs · reference.md · privacy-model.md
